newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent higher, but lacks short-term direction.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent higher, but lacks short-term direction.

text.p: Brent crude futures prices firmed on Monday in Asia, but were struggling to find direction, brokers said.
August Brent crude on SIMEX was last traded at $17.88 per barrel, up 12 cents from London which settled at $17.76.

Brokers said the trade on SIMEX was too light to indicate it was a reflection of sentiment on Monday. London and New York rose on Friday but failed to hold the highs after Iraq said it was not trying to delay Iraqi crude exports.
Brokers said the London and New York reaction was headline trading, as Iraq had made a few comments last week saying it was not trying to delay crude exports.
"They will export oil, its just a matter of the timing. This is just short term speculation and headline trading," one broker said.
NYMEX July crude futuers were last traded on ACCESS at $18.89, up six cents from New York while August was last traded at $19.12, up six.
